history.name: The prompt that inventories an existing codebase
history.description: `ledger bootstrap` prints a ready-to-use brief for a coding agent to survey a codebase that already exists and turn it into the first edition of a ledger. It sets the voice — every entry a present-tense statement of what the product does, never of who built it or when — has the agent propose the areas and wait for them to be confirmed, then work one area at a time, and says plainly what isn't worth an entry and to ask rather than guess where the code doesn't say what something is for. Surveying a codebase is work only something that can read it can do; this is what makes the result usable rather than invented.
history.dev_notes: assets/BOOTSTRAP.md, printed with {product} substituted; deliberately batched one area at a time, because a survey attempted in a single pass runs out of context and starts inventing.
